perOption.label: (A) born
perOption.reason: Past-participial adjunct 'Originally born in France' (reduced from '(being/having been) born in France') modifying the matrix subject Brunel. Dangling-modifier test passes: the implicit subject of 'born' = Brunel, who was indeed born in France. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (B) supplying
perOption.reason: Strip the fronted PP 'During the Napoleonic Wars': what remains is 'Brunel's factory supplying British troops with boots' — an NP plus a participial modifier with no finite verb, i.e., a sentence fragment. Alternative parses all fail: (i) absolute construction requires an accompanying matrix clause, none exists; (ii) reduced relative 'factory [which was] supplying...' still leaves no predicate; (iii) no other licensing construction. A finite verb is required: 'supplied' or 'was supplying'. Ungrammatical.

perOption.label: (C) buying
perOption.reason: 'stopped buying his boots' — stop + gerund (= cease the activity of buying) is the required complementation, and the cessation reading fits the discourse ('he went out of business'). Grammatical.

perOption.label: (D) because of
perOption.reason: 'because of' is a complex preposition governing an NP; 'his debt' is an NP. Plain 'because' would require a finite clause, so 'because of' is the correct form here. Grammatical.

perOption.label: (E) to move
perOption.reason: 'ways for people and goods to move across it' — infinitival relative on 'ways' with the for-phrase supplying the semantic (notional) subject of the infinitive. Standard construction. Grammatical.

note: Only (B) fails: removing the temporal adjunct exposes a verbless main clause (fragment). No alternative parse (absolute construction, reduced relative, inversion, etc.) rescues it. All other underlines are provably well-formed under their governing rules, so the answer set is a singleton.
